analysis.headline: A year after Carlos Manzo's killing, investigators tie the Uruapan mayor's murder to CJNG revenge and count 34 detained
analysis.what_happened: Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo was shot dead on 1 November 2025 by a 17-year-old, and authorities attribute the killing to the CJNG. El País and Infobae report an encrypted chat, a hard drive and 34 detentions, including people from his close circle.
analysis.says_vs_does: Excélsior reports investigators call the case 90% solved and describe it as CJNG revenge for the August 2025 arrest of plaza boss René Belmontes, El Rhino. Sources here do not say whether whoever ordered the killing has been charged.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The CJNG, in succession since El Mencho's death, lost its Uruapan plaza boss before the killing and dozens of operatives after it. Manzo's family and movement remain split over his political legacy, Contramuro and the Los Angeles Times report.
tensions: CJNG vs Uruapan's local government: the mayor confronted the group directly during his year in office, Milenio reports.
State prosecutors vs FGR: the federal prosecutor did not take over the case, according to Excélsior.

analysis.headline: Mexican outlets profile the four Mayiza operators sanctioned by the US Treasury as the faction fights the Chapitos and CJNG alliance
analysis.what_happened: Infobae, El Financiero and El Congresista profile four close operators of Ismael Zambada Sicairos, Mayito Flaco, sanctioned by the US Treasury. They include Francisco Javier Mendoza Uriarte, brother of El Güero Chompas, described as Mayito Flaco's secretary.
analysis.says_vs_does: A Treasury sanction is an administrative designation, not a criminal charge or an arrest. Noticias PV reports Treasury mapped the faction's new leadership and its laundering methods, while the Mayiza keeps fighting for Culiacán.
analysis.follow_the_money: Noticias PV describes laundering mechanisms in Sinaloa identified by Treasury. Sources do not give a figure for frozen assets or laundered sums.
analysis.at_stake: Sanctions raise the cost for banks and firms that deal with named operators. The Navy sent another 1,600 personnel to Sinaloa, and Navy Secretary Raymundo Morales visited Mazatlán to review the deployment.
tensions: Mayiza vs Chapitos and CJNG: the rival faction has been allied with the CJNG since mid-2025, El Financiero reports.

analysis.headline: Venezuela's army reportedly bombs an ELN camp in Apure, turning on a long-tolerated Colombian guerrilla ally
analysis.what_happened: El Mundo, citing Infobae, and CiberCuba report that the Venezuelan army bombed an ELN camp in Apure. Preliminary and officially unconfirmed reports speak of 19 dead.
analysis.says_vs_does: Caracas has not confirmed the strike in these sources, and the death toll is unverified. CiberCuba places the reported action amid Delcy Rodríguez's rapprochement with Washington, after decades of chavista tolerance for the ELN.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: An attack on the ELN gives the Rodríguez government a visible act against a group Washington targets. Across the border, Cúcuta faces nine gangs, with the Tren de Aragua charging Venezuelans who cross informal paths.
tensions: Venezuelan state vs ELN: a former rear-guard host has reportedly turned its air power on the guerrilla.
Tren de Aragua vs ELN and FARC dissidents: they compete over extortion and crossings in Cúcuta.

analysis.headline: Ecuador's fourth curfew of the year opens with 40 detentions in Guayaquil as a town cancels a contract tied to a Los Lobos financier
analysis.what_happened: A ten-day night curfew began in Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, El Oro and Esmeraldas after 33 night-time violent deaths. Primicias reports the armed forces detained 40 people in Guayaquil on day one for breaking it.
analysis.says_vs_does: Defense minister Gian Carlo Loffredo says the curfew aims to capture gang leaders and strangle their logistics. The first-day record shows detentions for curfew violations, and violence persisted through three earlier curfews this year.
analysis.follow_the_money: The mayor of Baba is ending a water and sewer contract with Consorcio Corporativo Baba, linked to Los Lobos financier Jackson Zambrano, Primicias reports. She says it passed every control and was supervised by BEDE and the European Investment Bank. Sources do not give the contract's value.
analysis.at_stake: The Noboa government seeks visible security results weeks before elections. A Los Lobos-linked firm cleared public controls on a development-bank-supervised contract, which exposes gaps in vetting.
tensions: Los Lobos vs Los Choneros: both now operate in Quito as well as on the coast, El Mostrador reports.

analysis.headline: US prosecutors indict an alleged CJNG tunnel engineer as CBP misses its usual release of monthly border seizure data
analysis.what_happened: Federal prosecutors in California indicted Luis Manuel Hernández Victoria, a Mexican engineer accused of designing a cross-border drug tunnel for the CJNG. Separately, 42 people were indicted in San Diego over methamphetamine smuggling tied to the Mexican Mafia.
analysis.says_vs_does: Breitbart credits Hernández with numerous tunnels, while Hindustan Times describes one sophisticated tunnel; both rest on an indictment, which is an accusation. WOLA notes CBP has not published last month's apprehension and drug seizure data, unusually late.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: The CJNG's FTO designation lets prosecutors frame tunnel building as support for a terrorist organization. Without CBP's monthly data, the public seizure record for the month is missing.
tensions: CJNG vs US border enforcement: tunnels move drugs under the line that ports of entry inspect.

analysis.headline: Guatemalan and Peruvian courts move on laundering cases involving a Chinese-origin defendant and a Binance-linked fraud network
analysis.what_happened: A Guatemalan anti-laundering judge changed the offence faced by a man of Chinese origin linked to possible laundering of more than Q40 million, La Hora reports. Peruvian police raided properties in Lima and Callao over a fraud network.
analysis.says_vs_does: La Hora does not say which lesser or different offence the judge applied. Peruvian prosecutors say the network received illicit funds through a front company and bought virtual assets on Binance; two suspects face seven-day preliminary detention.
analysis.follow_the_money: The Guatemalan case concerns more than Q40 million, La Hora reports. The Peruvian network received 231,969 dollars from frauds in seven countries, La República reports.
analysis.at_stake: Changing the charge alters the penalty exposure in Guatemala's case. The Peruvian case shows fraud proceeds routed through a front company into crypto.
tensions: Guatemalan prosecutors vs the defense: the judge's ruling narrows or shifts the case they brought.

analysis.headline: A year after Rio's deadliest police raid, Folha says the Comando Vermelho still holds Penha as terrorist-label proposals spread
analysis.what_happened: Folha writes that one year after Operação Contenção, the deadliest police action in Brazil, the CV still operates in Penha and has expanded to other states. Flávio Bolsonaro proposed classifying the PCC and CV as narcoterrorist organizations, Poder360 reports.
analysis.says_vs_does: Supporters present mass raids and terrorist labels as answers to the factions. Folha's account, an opinion piece, finds the CV's territorial hold intact a year after the raid.
analysis.follow_the_money: Sources do not give a figure.
analysis.at_stake: Public security sits at the center of Lula's fourth term, Poder360 reports. Paraguay, the first South American state to label the PCC and CV terrorists, is opening a US-backed anti-drug office in Asunción.
tensions: Lula government vs bolsonarista right: the right campaigns on terrorist designations and harsher sentencing.

arc_updates.text: A year after Carlos Manzo's killing, investigators attribute it to CJNG revenge for El Rhino's arrest and report 34 detentions.
Mexican outlets profiled four Mayiza operators sanctioned by the US Treasury, including Mayito Flaco's secretary, as the Navy added 1,600 personnel in Sinaloa.
Venezuela's army reportedly bombed an ELN camp in Apure, with unconfirmed reports of 19 dead.
Ecuador's ten-day curfew in five provinces opened with 40 detentions in Guayaquil, and Baba is ending a contract with a firm tied to a Los Lobos financier.
